vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.76.3

The skill bundle provides sophisticated Weibo automation but employs several high-risk behaviors and potential vulnerabilities. It uses AppleScript (macOS) and PowerShell (Windows) to simulate system-level keystrokes and manipulate the clipboard to bypass bot detection (found in `paste-from-clipboard.ts` and `copy-to-clipboard.ts`). The `SKILL.md` file contains prompt-injection-style instructions directing the AI agent to autonomously terminate Chrome processes (`pkill`) without user confirmation. Furthermore, `scripts/vendor/baoyu-md/src/utils/languages.ts` performs dynamic imports of JavaScript from a third-party CDN (cdn-doocs.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com), and `paste-from-clipboard.ts` is vulnerable to AppleScript injection via the `--app` argument. While these features support the stated goal of browser automation, they grant the agent excessive system control and introduce remote code execution risks.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions largely match a Weibo posting tool, but it accesses local Chrome profiles and invokes host utilities that are not fully declared, so there are coherent uses but some unexplained / under-documented privileges you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (post to Weibo, support Markdown articles via Chrome CDP) aligns with the included scripts: markdown conversion, CDP helpers, clipboard/paste utilities and weibo-specific post logic. Reusing a logged-in Chrome profile and using CDP is expected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to run TypeScript scripts in the skill's scripts/ folder which discover and read Chrome user-data directories (DevToolsActivePort) and may parse process lists. They also rely on system clipboard and synthetic keystroke tools (osascript, swift, xdotool, ydotool, wl-copy/xclip, powershell). Those actions go beyond simple HTTP API calls and access local browser state (cookies, sessions), which is necessary to reuse an already-authenticated session but expands the data surface and host-level capabilities.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only). Code files are bundled and executed via bun or npx as described. No network-download install URLs were used, which lowers supply-chain risk — but scripts use npx -y bun (which may invoke remote package tool behavior) and spawn system commands at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, which is consistent with using an existing Chrome session, but the code reads environment variables opportunistically (overrides for Chrome path/profile) and probes standard Chrome user-data locations. It also expects external system utilities (swift, osascript, xdotool, ydotool, wl-copy/xclip, powershell) that are not listed in the skill's declared required binaries — this mismatch is an under-documentation risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent platform-wide privileges. It reads local profile dirs and creates temporary files but does not modify other skills or agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill automates a real Chrome browser to post to Weibo and intentionally reuses your local Chrome profile (so you must be logged in). Before installing, consider:
- It will read your Chrome user-data directories and interact with the active browser session (cookies/sessions) — only install if you trust the code and want it to act as your logged-in browser.
- The scripts call host utilities (osascript/swift on macOS, xdotool/ydotool on Linux, wl-copy/xclip for clipboard, powershell on Windows) but the registry metadata only lists bun/npx; ensure you have the expected tools and understand the skill will fail or behave differently if they’re missing.
- Because it sends real paste keystrokes and can activate applications, test it first with a disposable Chrome profile or in an environment without sensitive accounts open.
- If you’re not comfortable with a skill reading DevToolsActivePort and scanning default Chrome profile paths, or running local native commands, don’t enable it or review the included source files yourself (they are bundled) to confirm there are no unexpected network endpoints or telemetry.
If you want higher assurance, run the scripts in a controlled environment, or ask the skill author for an explicit, minimal list of required host tools and a justification for accessing each Chrome profile path.
